answer: A farm that wants 33 keys thus forfeits 33 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the ripple seed, the mirror timing is verifiable from the haven record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 179 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
